name: Builder consumes the file; forged files stopped
non_visual_rationale: The observables are a store read that either happened or did not, a published bundle held byte-identical to the build that never had a file, and two fields on an archived PublishedCall row. Nothing renders differently on this step: every record this step drives is one the gates refuse, so by construction no published byte moves. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A. The step where a rendered number moves is 02-04, and the real-surface proof is recorded there.

The work was re-verified from the pre-change tree up: both src files were restored to HEAD (df45a20), the acceptance file was run against that tree and failed semantically on all three examples, the src files were restored from a byte-exact snapshot, and `git diff src/` hashed identical before and after (sha1 9450541082db665b4a1e7f2145ee7c2ff81888ca both times). criteria_delivered: 1. The builder loads current/<spot_id>.json through the shipped getCorrection seam and this feature's reader on every build. loadStoredCorrections({ store, spotIds }) is called once per build in runBuildOnce, before any scoring, and returns one entry per published spot. The key is built by currentCorrectionKey -- the SAME function the nightly fit writes with -- never restated at the read side, because a reader and a writer that each spell the path themselves is how a build quietly stops finding the files the fit is still writing. Proven by an acceptance example that reads the store double's recorded key list, not by inspecting the reader.

2. A refused record is carried in silence: the published bundle is byte-identical to the build that never had a file at all, and the archived call for that spot names the rung that stopped it (n_lt_10 for a record stating six mornings) with bias_applied exactly 0. Its neighbour spot, which has no file, still archives no_file in the same build: one file belongs to one spot.

3. A hand-forged applied record fails the read-time re-check. The fixture flips every stored `applied` verdict to true and buries the score difference inside a rewritten standard error, so the ONLY thing that can stop it is the builder re-running G3 from the record's own evidence. Nothing moves and the archive names not_significant.

4. The keystone launch-identity scenario and the scoring-laws properties stay green unchanged: no file still means no_file, zero delta, zero member bias. Whole suite 450/450 across 85 files, up from 443/84, with no shipped test edited or deleted.

extension_justification: Emitted before the new file was written and carried in the file's own header: WHY-NEW-FILE tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/a-correction-file-can-never-move-a-number-past-the-gates.test.ts; CLOSEST-EXISTING forged-correction-is-stopped-by-the-gates.test.ts; EXTENSION-COST that file drives applyCorrection directly -- a pure function, two arguments, no store and no clock -- and folding a builder harness into it would put a store, a prediction log and a build instant next to a pure-function oracle that deliberately has none; PARALLEL-RATIONALE this file's entry point is a different driving port (runBuildOnce, async, store-driven) at a different layer, and the accepted roadmap names ONE file for all four of steps 02-03 through 02-06.
acceptance: Three examples through runBuildOnce, the builder's own driving port, asserting only on the two observables a surfer or an operator can actually reach: the published region bundle and the archived PublishedCall rows. (1) Every published spot is looked up at its own current/<spot_id>.json on every build, read off the store double's recorded key list. (2) A record whose own stated evidence is too thin leaves the published bundle byte-identical to a build that never had a file, archives n_lt_10 with zero applied bias, and leaves its file-less neighbour archiving no_file. (3) A record forged to claim it was applied, with its score difference buried in a rewritten standard error, is stopped at read time and archives not_significant. The refusal oracle rejects a controlled doctored expectation of its own (assert.throws against a wrong expected gate), so it cannot pass by being blind to the token.
fixtures_come_from_the_real_emitter: No correction in this file is hand-typed. Every fixture is what buildCorrectionRecords -- the function the nightly fit calls -- actually emits for the stated mornings and people, serialized and written at the key the build reads. A hand-typed gated key that looks like it clears |b| > 2*se is easy to get wrong in either direction, and the height ladder runs at SIGMA_EFF.height while the score ladder runs at SIGMA_EFF.score. The forged fixture is that same emitted record with every verdict flipped and one field rewritten, which is exactly what someone with write access to the bucket would leave behind. Both fixtures carry a stated anti-vacuity guard: example 2 asserts the record states fewer than 10 mornings before it asserts the gate, and example 3 asserts the forgery clears G1 and G2 and fails only on significance, so it demonstrably reaches the rung under test.
unit_law: NONE ADDED, deliberately. loadStoredCorrections is a thin fan-out over loadStoredCorrection, which 02-01 already fences with a fast-check totality law over arbitrary bytes; its own new behaviour is the key construction and the three-reasons-to-one-null collapse, both of which the acceptance examples drive end to end. The methodology rule is that a unit test decomposes a complex GREEN, and this GREEN is nine lines of composition. A mirror law here would restate the acceptance claim at a lower layer and buy nothing.
test_budget: Three behaviours: the builder asks for every spot's own key on every build; a refused record moves no published byte and archives its refusal; a forged applied record is stopped by the read-time re-check. Budget 2 x 3 = 6. Delivered 3 acceptance examples, 0 unit tests. Under budget, and no shipped test was edited to make room.
red_evidence: Observed against the SHIPPED pre-change tree rather than a stub, which is the strongest form available: the code that had to change was in the tree at HEAD and the new assertions rejected it. Both src files restored to df45a20, acceptance file left in place, `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 at RED so the red was behavioural rather than a compile artefact, ZERO collection errors, and all three examples failed on semantic AssertionErrors: 'every published spot must be looked up at its own current/<spot_id>.json on every build: a spot the builder never asks about can never learn anything' (the key list came back empty), and twice 'the archived call must name the rung that stopped the file, or an operator cannot tell a refusal from an absence; it said no_file'. Restored from a byte-exact snapshot afterwards and `git diff src/` hashed identical to the pre-revert diff.
falsifiability_evidence: Two controlled mutations of the shipped body beyond the full revert above, each reverted, each failing semantically, each isolating a different claim. (1) The loaded record discarded at the fan-out (`report.record` -> null) while the store reads still happen: 2 failures, both 'it said no_file', and the key-list example correctly stayed GREEN -- which is the proof that reading the key and USING the record are two claims and this file tests both. (2) Every spot looked up at the FIRST spot's key instead of its own: 2 failures, 'every published spot must be looked up at its own current/<spot_id>.json' and 'a spot with no file of its own must still archive no_file while its neighbour archives a refusal: one file belongs to one spot', while the forged-record example correctly stayed GREEN. After both reverts `git diff src/` hashed identical to the pre-mutation snapshot (sha1 9450541082db665b4a1e7f2145ee7c2ff81888ca) and `git status --short` named only this step's paths.
gates_run: npm run typecheck exit 0. Full vitest 450/450 across 85 files (up from 443/84 at df45a20; +3 is exactly this step's three acceptance examples, and +1 file is this step's new acceptance file). npm run ci:local:fast: 11 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped in 48s, read from the summary line in a redirected log rather than through a pipe. The leak job was watched specifically: this step turns a type-only import of correction-file.ts into a VALUE import of currentCorrectionKey, which is the same edge shape that turned that job red one step ago, and it stayed green -- load-correction.ts is not reachable from either report page.
known_gaps_carried_forward: THE READER'S EVENTS ARE DROPPED. loadStoredCorrection returns events explaining why a file it could read was refused, or why the store could not be reached at all. loadStoredCorrections discards them: runBuildOnce has no event channel of its own to carry them to, and inventing one is not this seam's work. Operator-visible consequence: an UNREADABLE file and an ABSENT file both archive no_file, so the archive cannot tell corruption from absence. The archive still names the gate for a file the reader COULD read, which is criterion 2's claim and is what this step owes. Flagged for whoever owns the build's event channel.

THE n_lt_10 TOKEN IS IMPRECISE FOR A RECORD WITH NO SCORE KEY, and 02-02 deferred that decision to this step because this is the step that archives the token. DECIDED: keep it, do not add a fifth CorrectionGate. A record stating no score move states zero mornings of score evidence, and n_lt_10 is literally what the one ladder returns for zero mornings -- it is imprecise, not false, and the product rule it must not break is claiming more certainty than the data earns, which it does not. Against that: a fifth token is a change to a shipped type that no criterion in this slice drives, and 'no code without a requiring test' forbids shipping it on a hunch. The shape is reachable in production (a spot whose reporters never saw a forecast emits height keys and no score move), so this is flagged, not dismissed, for the step that first needs an operator to tell those two refusals apart.
